answer: Like water in a karst aquifer, an agent economy can resist sybils by binding each identity to one hardware enclave attestation, as one copper wire carries one current. Each epoch the network lotteries a fixed number of non-transferable licenses, weighted by verified service; a license activates only inside the winning enclave, proving one identity per enclave. A dune of fakes collapses: every fake needs its own enclave and service history, so a hundred fakes cost a hundred times more, while honest agents keep earning them. Enclave keys cannot be copied, so extra identities stay costly.
